title: They hurt you… in the place that taught you about love.
paragraphs: They hurt you… in the place that taught you about love.
And now there’s a question you’re too afraid to say out loud:
“Was God even there… when they broke me?”
The wound didn’t just come from people.
It came from people who knew Scripture.

People who lifted hands on Sunday…
but used their tongues like knives on Monday.
And now you’re left holding two things that don’t make sense together:
Somewhere deep inside, a lie started forming.
“If this is church… I don’t want God.”
Church hurt doesn’t just bruise your emotions.
It attacks your view of God.
It makes you question His goodness… because His people failed to reflect Him.
But don’t confuse representation with identity.
God is not the worst version of the people who claim His name.
God is not the worst version of the people who claim His name.
The Bible doesn’t hide this tension.

But it is you, a man like myself, my companion, my close friend.
With whom I once enjoyed sweet fellowship…”
This wasn’t betrayal from the outside.
Some scholars interpret this passage as David referring to a specific betrayal within his inner circle.
Others see it as a broader picture of relational betrayal among God’s people.
The Bible is not naïve about church hurt.
And here’s what will shake you:

“Now the betrayer had arranged a signal with them: ‘The one I kiss is the man; arrest him.’
Going at once to Jesus, Judas said, ‘Greetings, Rabbi!’ and kissed him.
Jesus replied, ‘Do what you came for, friend.’”
“The Lord turned and looked straight at Peter…”
So if you’ve been wounded by people in the church…
Because if you stop the story at betrayal…
Not just what they did to you…
But what lives in all of us.
“For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.”
That includes the ones who hurt you.
We don’t just suffer from sin.
And this is why Jesus didn’t come to build a perfect social circle.
You and I are separated from God because of sin.
No amount of church attendance, service, or good behavior can fix that.
“For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—not by works, so that no one can boast.”
And that grace was purchased through blood.
Jesus Christ lived the life we failed to live.
Then He died the death we deserved.

“But He was pierced for our transgressions,
He was crushed for our iniquities;
the punishment that brought us peace was on Him,
and by His wounds we are healed.”
Your healing will never come from perfect people.
It comes from a pierced Savior.
So what do you do with church hurt?
You don’t build your identity around it.
Because if you let people push you away from Christ…
and then your distance from God keeps you wounded.
But if you bring your pain to Jesus…
That same place of betrayal becomes a doorway to deeper intimacy with Him.
Church hurt is not proof that God failed you.
It’s proof that humanity still needs a Savior.
Not to go back to fake smiles.
But to come back to Christ.
The One who will never gossip about you…
“The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit.”
What are you going to do with your pain?
Will you let it harden you?
Or will you let it lead you… back to Jesus?
If you’re tired of carrying this alone…
If you’re done letting wounds define your faith…
If something in your spirit is saying, “I need Him again…”
“Jesus… I’ve been hurt. But I don’t want to walk away from You. Heal me. Restore me. Teach me how to trust again.”
Find people who don’t pretend to be perfect—
but are serious about following Christ.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
